sources.title: Renew Your NSP Scholarship 2026
sources.text:
Reviewed on 2026-09-01 by Dr. Shrawan Kumar Pathak.

Quick Reply: Renew your NSP scholarship on scholarships.gov.in: log in with your existing 14-digit OTR, choose Renewal, update your academic details, confirm your Aadhaar-seeded bank account, and submit before your scheme's closing date. Then your institute must verify it. Miss the window and you lose the year.

The clock is the enemy here, not the form. A renewal takes ten honest minutes, but the scholarship slips away in the days you let it sit. The portal opened for the 2026-27 academic year on 1 June 2026, and every scheme runs its own closing date after that. So treat this as a countdown, not a chore.

First, mark your deadline today

NSP does not set one single last date for the whole country. Each scheme, your pre-matric, post-matric, merit-cum-means or central-sector award, announces its own renewal closing date on the portal. That is the only date that matters to you.

So before you read another word, do this: open scholarships.gov.in, find your scheme, and write its closing date on your phone calendar with a reminder three days earlier. If a date is not yet shown for your scheme, check back weekly. Never trust a date from a coaching blog or a forwarded message. Verify the exact closing date for your scheme on scholarships.gov.in.

Why the urgency? A renewal that is not submitted and verified in time cannot be revived later. You either reapply as a fresh candidate next year, if the scheme even allows it, or you simply lose this year's money.

What renewal actually means

Renewal is only for students who already received this scholarship last year and are continuing the same course. You do not build a new profile. You do not create a second login. You carry forward the One Time Registration you already have.

Your OTR is a unique 14-digit number tied to your Aadhaar, and it stays with you for your whole academic career. That is the thread the system follows from one year to the next.

One trap to avoid: do not file a fresh application by mistake. A duplicate fresh-plus-renewal pair gets rejected, and untangling that wastes the very days you cannot spare.

Be ready before you log in

Have these in hand so you do not stall halfway:

 Your OTR number or registered application ID and password.

 Your last passed examination marksheet, showing you were promoted.

 Your current bank passbook, with an Aadhaar-seeded account active for DBT.

 Your current course, year and institute details.

If your last marksheet has an error, fix it before you renew, do not submit on a wrong record. Our guide on what to do when a marksheet correction is rejected walks through that. Lost the marksheet itself? See how to get a duplicate marksheet using RTI quickly.

The renewal steps, in order

Step 1: Log in with your OTR

Go to scholarships.gov.in, click Login, and enter your OTR or application ID and password. Choose the Renewal option, not fresh application. If you have forgotten your password, reset it the same day, password recovery is not something to leave for the deadline evening.

Step 2: Update your academic details

Enter your new class or year, your latest marks and your current institute. This is where the scheme checks that you were promoted and still meet its progression rule (minimum marks or attendance, as your scheme defines). Be exact, mismatched numbers invite a defective-application flag.

Step 3: Confirm your bank and Aadhaar seeding

Your money arrives only through Direct Benefit Transfer into an Aadhaar-seeded bank account. Use the portal's Check Aadhaar Seeding Status tool. If it is not seeded, walk into your bank branch and seed it now, a payout cannot land in an unseeded account no matter how perfect your application is.

Step 4: Submit and save the proof

Submit before your scheme's closing date and download the acknowledgement. Screenshot the submitted status too. That timestamp is your evidence if anything goes wrong downstream.

After you submit: the verification chain

Submitting is not the finish line. Your renewal now travels through a chain, and the first link is the one that most often jams.

Institute verification (Level 1). Your school or college nodal officer must verify your renewal on NSP. This is the usual choke point, especially close to the cut-off.

Nodal officer verification. It then moves to the District, State or Ministry nodal officer (DNO, SNO, MNO) depending on the scheme.

Payment. Once cleared, the amount is released through PFMS into your Aadhaar-seeded account. Use Track Your Payment on the portal to follow it.

So after submitting, do not relax. Confirm within a few days that your institute has actually verified you. A renewal sitting unverified at the institute on the closing date is as good as not submitted.

Figure: step-by-step flow. If a step stalls, use the grievance or RTI route shown.

If your renewal is stuck or rejected

When the institute sits on your application or it is rejected without a clear reason, move fast, the deadline does not pause for your problem.

Chase the institute first. Ask your scholarship nodal officer to verify it and keep a dated written request (email or letter).

Raise a grievance on NSP. Use Grievance Registration on scholarships.gov.in and keep the ticket number.

Call the NSP Helpdesk. Phone 0120-6619540 (8:00 AM to 8:00 PM, all days except government holidays) or email helpdesk[at]nsp[dot]gov[dot]in. Payment-only queries go to the PFMS helpdesk.

File an RTI. If the institute or nodal office still gives no answer, file an RTI asking why your verified renewal is pending or rejected and on what date it was acted on. A public college or government school is a public authority, and an RTI usually breaks a silent file open.

The RTI route is powerful because it forces a dated, written reason. If you have hit walls before with an institution that ignored requests, the same discipline that works for degree verification through RTI works here.

A quick word on money in the gap

If a delayed renewal leaves a funding gap, do not stop attending. Know your repayment and pause rights on any study loan so a short delay does not snowball, our explainer on education loan moratorium rights covers the breathing room you are entitled to.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a new OTR every year to renew?

No. Your 14-digit OTR is issued once on your Aadhaar and lasts your whole academic career. For renewal you log in with the same OTR and only update your academic details. Creating a second profile causes rejection.

What is the last date to renew my NSP scholarship in 2026?

There is no single all-India date. The portal opened for 2026-27 on 1 June 2026, and each scheme announces its own closing date. Check the exact closing date for your scheme on scholarships.gov.in and set a reminder.

Can I renew if I failed or was not promoted?

Generally no. Renewal requires you to have been promoted to the next class or year and to meet your scheme's progression rule, such as minimum marks or attendance. Confirm your scheme's exact rule on the portal before you apply.

Why has my renewal not been paid even after I submitted?

Submission is only the start. Your institute must verify it, then the nodal officer, then PFMS releases the payment. Check that your institute has verified you and that your bank account is Aadhaar-seeded for DBT.

My college has not verified my renewal. What do I do?

Send your nodal officer a dated written request, then raise a grievance on NSP and note the ticket number. If it stays stuck, call the NSP Helpdesk, and if there is still no answer, file an RTI asking why your renewal is pending.

My bank account is not Aadhaar-seeded. Will I still get paid?

No. NSP pays only into an Aadhaar-seeded account through DBT. Use Check Aadhaar Seeding Status on the portal, and if it is not seeded, visit your bank branch to seed it before the closing date.

Can I switch my bank account during renewal?

You can update bank details, but the new account must be Aadhaar-seeded and active for DBT. Verify the current process for changing payout details on scholarships.gov.in, and confirm seeding before you submit so the payment does not bounce.

NSP Scholarship Last Date 2026-27: The Deadlines That Matter Now
The National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in) has been open for the academic year 2026-27 since 1 June 2026. Two deadlines are now close:

Pre-matric scholarships: 30 September 2026 (extended from 31 August 2026)
Post-matric and higher-education scholarships: 31 October 2026

Institute (L1) verification runs up to 15 November 2026 and L2 verification up to 30 November 2026. An application that is submitted but never verified by your school or college is as good as rejected, so submitting early matters more than submitting at all.

Stage
Last date

Pre-matric application
30 September 2026

Post-matric application
31 October 2026

Institute (L1) verification
15 November 2026

L2 verification (District / State / Ministry)
30 November 2026

A caution before you read further: the official portal publishes dates only for some schemes on its front page. Other dates come from reliable education portals and have been cross-checked, but deadlines on NSP are extended fairly often, pre-matric has already been extended once this cycle. Always confirm the date inside the scheme's own guideline after you log in.
The Big Rule Change for 2026-27
The official portal now states: "Students may apply for one merit-based scholarship scheme and one or more welfare-based scholarship schemes from AY 2026-27, as per scheme eligibility criteria."
This replaces the old "only one scholarship" rule that many websites still print. In practice:

A merit-based scheme uses your single merit slot, for example AICTE Pragati, or PM-YASASVI.
Welfare-based schemes, such as AICTE Saksham and Swanath, can be combined with a merit scheme.

Check the individual scheme guideline before assuming two schemes can be combined.
PM-USP CSSS: Renewal Window Open till 31 October
The official portal currently shows renewal applications open for:

PM-USP Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students (CSSS)
PM-USP Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu Kashmir and Ladakh

Earlier reports had said 30 September for CSSS renewal, the official portal now shows 31 October 2026. Fresh CSSS applications appear to be closed for this cycle; the portal's notice refers only to renewals.

Note for AICTE schemes: each has a separate Degree and Diploma variant. Applying under the wrong variant is a known reason for rejection.
NMMSS: Closing 30 September 2026
The National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme deadline was extended by the Ministry of Education from 31 August to 30 September 2026.

For Class 9 students in government, government-aided or local body schools

Family income up to ₹3.5 lakh a year
Must have cleared the state-conducted NMMS exam
₹12,000 a year, payable from Class 9 to Class 12
1 lakh fresh scholarships every year

OTR, Aadhaar and Face Authentication
This is where most applications get stuck.

One Time Registration (OTR) is mandatory for all NSP services. Your OTR number becomes your login username and stays valid through your academic career.
Face authentication is mandatory to generate the OTR. You need the UIDAI AadhaarFaceRD app and the NSP OTR app, and a live face capture that matches your Aadhaar photo.
You need a mobile number linked to Aadhaar for the OTP.
No Aadhaar? You may use the Aadhaar enrolment slip, or a parent's or guardian's Aadhaar if you are a minor.
Your bank account must be Aadhaar-seeded through NPCI, otherwise the money will not reach you. Check it under Profile Details, and use NPCI's Bharat Aadhaar Seeding Enabler (BASE) platform to seed it yourself. Allow 24 to 48 hours.
If face authentication fails with Error 904, update the AadhaarFaceRD app from the Play Store. A biometric lock on your Aadhaar will also block it and must be unlocked first.
You can complete NSP work at a Common Service Centre for ₹30 per candidate.

Disabled students must first log in to the UDID portal and give consent to share UDID details, and only then apply on NSP.
Documents You Need

Aadhaar card (or enrolment slip / parent's Aadhaar for minors)
Bank passbook or cancelled cheque, with the account Aadhaar-seeded
Income certificate from a revenue authority such as the Tehsildar or SDM, Form 16 is not accepted, and the certificate must be from the current financial year
Caste, community, tribe or minority certificate, as applicable
Disability certificate and UDID, for disability schemes
Previous year's marksheet
Bonafide certificate from the institution
Fee receipt
Passport-size photograph
Admission letter, for Top Class schemes

Uploads are normally PDF or JPEG, up to 200 KB each, and must be legible. Limits can vary by scheme.
How to Apply: Step by Step

Create your OTR at scholarships.gov.in using Aadhaar, an Aadhaar-linked mobile number and face authentication.
Seed your bank account with Aadhaar through NPCI before you apply.
Log in with your OTR number and password.
Choose Fresh or Renewal correctly, this is a common cause of rejection.
Select your scheme, keeping the one-merit-plus-welfare rule in mind, and pick the right Degree or Diploma variant.
Fill in personal, academic, institutional and income details.
Upload your documents in the correct format and size.
Submit, no edits are possible after final submission, and save your Application ID.
Follow up with your Institute Nodal Officer for L1 verification. This is the step students most often forget.
Track your status on the NSP dashboard.

Why Applications Get Rejected

Bank account not Aadhaar-seeded on NPCI, or wrong account number or IFSC
Income certificate stale, or from the wrong authority, or Form 16 submitted instead
The institute never verified the application at L1
Applying as Fresh when it should be Renewal, or the reverse
Wrong scheme or wrong Degree/Diploma variant
Documents illegible, cropped, or over the size limit
Family income above the scheme ceiling
Name on Aadhaar not matching school or college records
Already holding another scholarship where the scheme does not allow it

Two Things to Check Before You Assume Your Scheme Is Live
Post-matric SC/ST/OBC scholarships are centrally sponsored but implemented by states, and in many states the application does not go through NSP. For example: Bihar (scstpmsonline.bihar.gov.in), Uttar Pradesh (scholarship.up.gov.in), Karnataka (ssp.karnataka.gov.in) and Maharashtra (mahadbt.maharashtra.gov.in). Check your own state portal.
Minority scholarships, the pre-matric, post-matric and merit-cum-means schemes for minorities, have a disputed status. The Centre told Parliament in July 2026 that there have been no fresh admissions under these schemes since 2022-23. They did not appear among the schemes with published 2026-27 dates. Do not rely on websites claiming these are open until you see it on the official portal.
State Deadlines Worth Noting

Uttar Pradesh (scholarship.up.gov.in): Dashmottar / post-matric fresh 31 October 2026, renewal 15 October 2026. OTR with Aadhaar e-KYC is mandatory, and the printed hard copy usually has to reach your institution within a few days of final lock.
Karnataka (ssp.karnataka.gov.in): pre-matric closes 30 September 2026; post-matric dates vary by department, with some running to January 2027. SATS ID is mandatory.
Several state schemes hosted on NSP close between October and December 2026, including schemes in Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Maharashtra, Meghalaya and the UTs.

Helpline

Help with
Contact

NSP portal
0120-6619540 (8:00 AM to 8:00 PM, except government holidays)

NSP email
[email protected]

Payment issues (PFMS)
1800 118 111 (toll free)

PFMS email
[email protected]

Frequently Asked Questions
Q1. What is the last date for NSP scholarship 2026-27?
30 September 2026 for pre-matric schemes and 31 October 2026 for post-matric schemes, as per current information. Dates can be extended.
Q2. Can I apply for two scholarships this year?
Yes, within limits. From 2026-27 you may apply for one merit-based scheme and one or more welfare-based schemes, subject to each scheme's rules.
Q3. Is face authentication compulsory?
Yes, for generating the OTR. You need the AadhaarFaceRD app and the NSP OTR app, and a mobile number linked to Aadhaar.
Q4. My application was submitted but shows no progress. Why?
Most likely your institute has not completed L1 verification. Contact your Institute Nodal Officer, and escalate to the Principal if needed. L1 verification closes on 15 November 2026.
Q5. What if the money does not reach my account?
The most common reason is that the bank account is not Aadhaar-seeded with NPCI. Seed it through NPCI BASE or at your bank branch, then contact the PFMS helpline.
Q6. Is Form 16 accepted as an income certificate?
No. You need an income certificate from a competent revenue authority such as the Tehsildar or SDM, issued in the current financial year.
Q7. What if I miss the deadline?
There is no offline route. If a scheme is extended you can still apply, but do not count on it, apply before the current last date.
Conclusion
With pre-matric closing on 30 September and post-matric on 31 October 2026, this is the period to finish your NSP application, not to start it. Complete your OTR and Aadhaar seeding first, submit with a valid income certificate, and then chase your institute for verification before 15 November. Re-check scholarships.gov.in for extensions, since the portal has extended deadlines more than once in past years.
Disclaimer: Verified as of 19 September 2026 from the official National Scholarship Portal and reliable education sources. NSP deadlines are extended frequently, and only some scheme dates are published on the portal's front page. Always confirm the last date inside your scheme's own guideline at scholarships.gov.in.

sources.text:
After secondary education, the Post-Matric Scholarship serves as financial aid for students who want to pursue their education further. They can apply for the Post-Matric Scholarship 2026-27 through the National Scholarship Portal. The NSP registrations for the post-matric scholarship are accepted through the official website, scholarships.gov.in. The Post-Matric Scholarship for Students with Disabilities for the academic year 2026-27 commenced on June 1, 2026. The last date to submit applications is October 31, 2026.
 This Story also ContainsPost Matric Scholarship 2026-27 - Eligibility CriteriaPost Matric Scholarship 2026-27 - DatesPost-Matric Scholarship 2026-27 - Application ProcessPost Matric Scholarship 2026-27 - Renewal ApplicationsPost Matric Scholarship 2026-27 - Documents RequiredBenefits of Post-Matric Scholarship 2026-27

 Post Matric Scholarship 2026-27

 Eligible students can apply as fresh/renewal applicants through the official post-matric scholarship portal. Post-matric scholarship benefits apply to all acknowledged schools/institutions offering classes from 11 onwards, as well as full-time and distance education courses for post-graduate degree/diploma programs.
